/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 6

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


open SimpleGraph

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture6
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 6](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a connected graph `G` we have
`Ls(G) ≥ 1 + n(G) - m(G) - a(G)` where `a(G)` is defined via independent sets.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture6 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    1 + (Fintype.card α : ℝ) - matchingNumber G - α(G) ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture6

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 6 and surrounding remarks: https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

Author’s definition/reference script, especially invariant entries 1, 2, 3, 5 and conjecture entry 6: https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534js_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js (served capture dated 23 July 2026)
Written on the Wall II introduction and bibliography: http://web.archive.org/web/20241118002601/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/list.htm

E. DeLaViña and B. Waller, Spanning Trees with Many Leaves and Average Distance, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 15 (2008), R33, introduction and references; read via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v15i1r33/pdf
review.notes: The sole theorem matches the source’s bound L_s(G) ≥ 1 + n − μ(G) − α(G). The author’s definitions confirm maximum matching size, independence number, and the maximum count of degree-one vertices over spanning trees. The source credits DeLaVina (1996) and marks the result proved, agreeing with research solved. Nontrivial excludes the singleton degeneracy; the surrounding source discussion of these leaf bounds explicitly identifies the n > 1 restriction. Scratch Lean checks established finite-maximum attainment and independently proved μ(K₂)=1, α(K₂)=1, L_s(K₂)=2 and the full inequality at K₂, without sorry. The original 1996 proof PDF was unavailable, but the official archived statement, definitions, and status were accessible. The final scratch compilation succeeded; the reviewed file was unchanged.
